thesis: This episode argues that Anthropic's revenue growth from $9B to $30B run rate is driven by non-slowing returns to frontier intelligence in enterprise, where customers invest heavily in tokens with newer models. It posits that scaling laws and model capability improvements continue to unlock significant value, with Anthropic viewing itself as a platform that accrues value while its customers accrue even more.

claims.quote: From what we see the scaling laws are not slowing down. So if that's true, you said before it's hard for humans to be exponential in their thinking and not linear that continues to be true for however many more turns of the crank here.

claims.claim: Anthropic has a dynamic way of looking at near-term and medium to long-term compute, optimizing for price performance over time.
claims.quote: But we have a pretty dynamic way of looking at near-term compute and then medium to long-term compute. But the things we're assessing are largely the same. What is different is just the time horizon.

claims.claim: Anthropic believes that getting more compute would be deployed very rapidly across different use cases today.
claims.quote: I would say today that getting a bunch more compute, I think it would be deployed very rapidly across those different use cases.

claims.claim: Anthropic thinks that most of what they are building is a platform that can accrue a lot of value while customers building on that platform can accrue even more value.
claims.quote: The way I would think about it is most of what we're building is platform. We think that there's so many examples of where a platform can accrue a lot of value, but the customers who are building on that platform actually can even more value.

claims.claim: Anthropic believes the returns to frontier intelligence are extremely high, especially in enterprise, and that releasing new models unlocks more TAM and use cases.
claims.quote: we want to continue to make that long-term investment in developing the best models because we think the returns to frontier intelligence are extremely high and it's extremely high, especially in enterprise.

claims.claim: Anthropic sees huge improvements in capability and model efficiency with each new model release, such as going from Opus 4 to 4.5, 4.6, and now 4.7.
claims.quote: And so if you look at going from Opus 4 to 4.5, 4.6 and now 4.7, they're not equal but each one of those leaps to a new model has a multiplier in terms of how much more efficient it is at processing tokens effectively.

claims.claim: Anthropic's revenue grew from about $9 billion of run rate revenue at the start of the year to $30 billion of run rate revenue by the end of the quarter, enabled by model intelligence leaps.
claims.quote: We started the year with about $9 billion of run rate revenue and we ended the quarter with $30 billion of run rate revenue. That kind of a change is really enabled by these model intelligence leaps and then the products that we build around them.

claims.claim: Anthropic believes that in enterprise, the returns to frontier intelligence are not slowing down, and that customers invest heavily in more tokens with newer models.
claims.quote: And that's a court thesis of our business that especially in enterprise, the returns to frontier intelligence are not slowing down.
